chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Pianist and arranger for Billie Holiday after Bobby Tucker
summary: Horace replaced Bobby Tucker as Billie Holiday's pianist and condensed her big-band charts for six pieces, including Strange Fruit, impressing her and her husband John Levy.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: We talked one evening about a short period where you worked with Billie Holiday. Do you want to tell me a little bit about that?
Yes. That was in New York City. I made quite a few things for Billie.

Arrangements, and I played piano for her. I followed a guy that's an excellent pianist. He was with her for quite some time -- Bobby Tucker who now is Billy Eckstine's Eckstein's pianist. He's been with him for quite a few years. Well, he was with Billie Holiday previous to that, so he left

Billie Holiday, and went with Billy Eckstine, so I took his place, and she came down to hear my group where we were playing, and we were playing a theatre, and what knocked Billie out, I think, where I'm concerned -- where I was concerned, rather, is the fact that she had some music, and it was for a big band, and it hadn't been condensed where six pieces could play, so what I would do, I would look at all the parts, and where there would be seven bars out, with this particular horn, what's important, you know, I would suggest to fill that in with the other guys and make it full, and that knocked her out. She says -- she turned round to her husband, John Levy, and says, "See John, this is it. This is it," you know. But she liked that. She had her faculties, you know, and I made some things for her like "Strange Fruit." And Bobby Tucker had made a swinging thing for her that I had to condense called "Them Their Eyes," Lady Day. And I really had a ball with her, and it was a different experience from Lena Horne. Just -- they were two different personalities.
Was this after you had worked with Lena Horne?
So this would be somewhere in the forties?
